subject: Hosted API pricing — volume discount structure and protections
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex@helixlabs.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixlabs.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0000
Subject: Hosted API pricing — initial volume tiers and protections

Alex / Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — glad the team at Helix is moving toward a production rollout. Per our conversation, I wanted to put an initial commercial outline on the table so you have something concrete to review with procurement. High-level proposal for Hosted API (usage-based, per-token):

- Commit tier: $250k monthly committed spend for 12 months (preferred)
- Marginal per-token rates (post-commit): 0–500M tokens @ $0.00085 / token; 500M+ @ $0.00065 / token
- Overage: metered at marginal rates above; credits to be applied to monthly invoices
- Price lock: 12 months from contract signature for the rates above

We typically limit MFN clauses to published public API pricing (not private, bespoke deals) and keep them scoped by comparable commit size. CPI-style indexing is not something we commonly expose beyond modest annual escalators — we can cap escalators in the contract if needed.

If you can share the specifics of Helix's target commit horizon and whether you need an MFN that covers all competitors vs. public list pricing, I'll get legal and finance engaged and circulate a short exhibit.

Next steps: if this looks directionally right, I can send a pricing exhibit + SOW and propose a procurement call early next week.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0178

Attachment stub: pricing-exhibit-v1.pdf (see full exhibit attached in follow-up)
From: Alex Kim <alex@helixlabs.com>

Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 18:41:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — initial volume tiers and protections

Monica,

Thanks for the clear starter — helpful. A few asks from procurement and finance up front:

1) MFN: Helix needs a Most-Favored-Nation clause that covers any published commercial offering for Host API customers of comparable scale. We rely on this to avoid being disadvantaged as we commit spend over a multi-year rollout.
2) Price lock: willing to commit to a 24-month lock given expected spend ramp. Can Redwood accommodate 24 months?
3) CPI cap: because we have tight annual budgets, we need a hard cap on annual price changes tied to CPI (Helix would prefer <= 1.5% / year).

If Redwood can sign to MFN + 24-month lock + CPI cap at ~1.5% we can move quickly — procurement is asking for an exhibit we can feed into our SOW and legal team.

Appreciate the quick movement here.

—Alex
Alex Kim

FYI — procurement at Helix is pushing for a broad MFN, a 24-month price lock and a CPI cap at 1.5%. Forwarding Alex's note (below). Can you advise on legal/finance appetite and possible guardrails? My read: we can probably offer a compromise but need to be careful with MFN scope.

Key constraints to consider:
- MFN carveouts for private, custom deals and passthrough channel pricing
- MFN tied to similar committed spend/term (no unconditional parity to single-call discounts)
- CPI cap: we support a small, fixed cap but 1.5% is tight — historically finance prefers ~2–3% or fixed step increases

If you can propose language we can send back in an exhibit that keeps the deal moving, that would be ideal.

Thanks — Monica

Monica — quick thoughts from pricing/legal side:

1) MFN: we can agree to an MFN but must scope it narrowly. Proposed guardrails: MFN applies only to published public API list prices and to competing hosted API offerings for customers with a similar committed monthly spend (within +/- 25%). Excludes bespoke private deployments, strategic partner deals, and channel/reseller pricing.

2) Price lock: we can extend to 18 months (mid-point), but 24 months requires exec approval because it increases revenue predictability risk. Offer: 18 months guaranteed lock with a one-time optional extension review at month 12 if Helix commits to a documented ramp schedule.

3) CPI cap: we typically avoid CPI indexing because models vary by geography, but we'll offer a hard cap of 2% annual price increase for the locked period. We can accept 1.5% for the first 12 months only if Helix ups the commit to $300k/month.

If you want, I can draft exhibit language that reflects these concessions and a short justification paragraph for legal.

—Rishi
VP, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com
From: Alex Kim <alex@helixlabs.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@helixlabs.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 08:21:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — initial volume tiers and protections

Monica / Rishi,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and constructive compromise. A couple of points from Helix:

- MFN: Helix cannot accept MFN limited only to "published list prices" — our concern is that Redwood could run rolling promotions or partner discounts that materially affect our unit economics. We need the MFN to cover any customer-facing prices for comparable commit sizes, including short-term promotions, for at least the first 12 months of the agreement.

- 18-month lock + conditional extension is reasonable, but procurement prefers certainty over options. If Redwood can do 18 months firm plus a 6-month administrative review clause, Helix will accept (so effectively 18–24 months with a simple review).

- CPI cap: Helix will accept 2% only if Redwood provides a one-time implementation credit equal to 5% of the first month invoice as a goodwill gesture; otherwise we hold at 1.5%.

Procurement timeline: we'd like to turn this into an executable exhibit by end of next week; legal will need clean exhibit language and a simple signature-ready attachable PDF.

—Alex
